peterkaminski / Flickr
ORCL Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

Oracle has become one of the largest AI infrastructure builders in the world, with a cloud business scaling rapidly on the back of multi-year contracts from major AI customers. Cloud Infrastructure revenue grew 93% in the fiscal fourth quarter, and Remaining Performance Obligations, the contracted backlog investors watch most closely, jumped 363% year over year to $638 billion.

The dislocation between price and target has widened through the summer. Whether Wall Street is stubbornly clinging to stale targets, or whether the market has overshot to the downside, is the question worth answering before Oracle reports later this week.

Cloud Buildout Costs Turned Investors Cautious

The most immediate driver of the derating has been the sheer scale of Oracle's capital spending program. Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 came in at negative $23.69 billion, on capital expenditures of $55.663 billion. Total liabilities reached $218.703 billion, and management guided to roughly $40 billion in fresh debt and equity funding across fiscal 2027, including a $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance already underway. Net cash capex for fiscal 2027 is expected around $70 billion.

title: Evercore Warns AI IPOs Could Pressure These Struggling Stocks. IBM and AppLovin Face Different Tests
detail:
Evercore Warns AI IPOs Could Pressure These Struggling Stocks. IBM and AppLovin Face Different Tests
Habib Ur Rehman
Mon, September 7, 2026 at 3:45 PM CDT 3 min read
IBM
APP
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors seeking a slice of a possible blockbuster AI flotation might sell something they already own to pay for it. That is the portfolio risk behind Evercore ISI's warning reported September 7. International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM) and AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) appeared on its screen of potential casualties.

Julian Emanuel's team identified underperformers with negative earnings-revision trends that could face additional pressure as investors prepare for possible OpenAI and Anthropic listings and seasonal tax-loss selling. The screen describes vulnerability. It does not establish that a fund has sold either stock to finance an IPO, or that those listings will happen on a fixed timetable.

Evercore Warns AI IPOs Could Pressure These Struggling Stocks. IBM and AppLovin Face Different Tests
The same selling pressure would meet different businesses

For International Business Machines Corporation (NYSE:IBM), the challenge is restoring operating momentum. Its second-quarter results showed software revenue growing 5% to $7.8 billion, with Red Hat up 11%. Hybrid cloud remains a plausible way to benefit as enterprises deploy AI across existing systems, rather than abandoning their infrastructure wholesale.

Yet infrastructure revenue fell 7%, with IBM Z down 42%. Free cash flow declined $300 million to $2.5 billion. A portfolio-driven selloff would therefore arrive while investors already have reasons to question execution. The bullish rebuttal requires improving business results, not merely arguing that the stock has fallen enough.

AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ:APP) presents a different tension. Its June-quarter revenue rose 53% to $1.924 billion, and it generated $863.3 million of free cash flow. Its advertising platform gives investors an existing commercial application of AI, with customers paying for measurable marketing outcomes. That cash generation could support resilience even if enthusiasm shifts toward newly listed AI developers.

The risk is sustaining those results in a competitive advertising market while scaling to new customers. Management explicitly flags forecasting, competition and execution risks. Strong historical growth cannot guarantee future returns, and a share-price decline does not independently prove undervaluation. Conversely, investor demand for a new AI listing does not by itself reduce the returns advertisers earn from AppLovin's existing service.

Q2 filings showed no broad retreat from these stocks

Insider Monkey counted 74 IBM holders at June 30 versus 59 at March 31. AQR Capital Management increased IBM shares approximately 42% to 2,688,952. AppLovin's count fell from 91 to 88, while Kensico Capital reduced its shares approximately 3.1% to 3,182,850. Neither disclosure establishes an IPO-related motive.

The upcoming initial public offerings (IPOs) of OpenAI and Anthropic may exacerbate the woes of already struggling stocks post-Labor Day, said strategists at Evercore ISI, spearheaded by Julian Emanuel.

Evercore sees further upside for AI stocks but warns that upcoming IPOs and seasonal tax-loss selling could accelerate the unloading of weaker AI-related stocks. The strategists at Evercore elucidated that investors may "make room" for these IPOs in their portfolios by reducing existing holdings, MarketWatch reported on Monday.

This trend is particularly relevant in the post-Labor Day market, with the mutual fund tax-loss selling season approaching in October. As this season nears, investors may sell underperforming stocks to realize losses, offset capital gains and lower tax bills. They could then redirect those proceeds toward anticipated blockbuster AI IPOs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, increasing pressure on weak performers.

Anticipating this portfolio shift, Evercore screened the Russell 3000 RUA for stocks meeting specific criteria: a market capitalization above $5 billion, a year-to-date decline of at least 10%, a gain of less than 20% from their 2026 low, and negative earnings-revision trends over the past three months.

Some of the names shortlisted in this category of 40 stocks are International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM), AppLovin (NASDAQ:APP), Tesla Inc. (NASDAQ:TSLA), AST SpaceMobile Inc. (NASDAQ:ASTS), McDonald's Corp. (NYSE:MCD) and First Solar Inc. (NASDAQ:FSLR).

Read Also:OpenAI Scientist Sounds the Alarm on AI, Warns 'No One Is Prepared' for What Comes Next — Hopes for 'Voluntary Slowdowns' in AI Development

Anthropic, OpenAI Race Toward Bigger Valuations

Anthropic is gearing up for its IPO in the coming weeks and is reportedly targeting a $2 trillion valuation and up to $100 billion from a potential IPO, surpassing Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) figures. The Claude maker also sees a $30 trillion revenue opportunity, though experts question such massive TAM projections. Anthropic more than doubled Q2 revenue to $11.6 billion and could go public as early as October.

Meanwhile, OpenAI's ChatGPT advertising business reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate within 200 days. The Sam Altman-led company plans to expand ads to over 40 countries, including India, as it diversifies revenue ahead of a potential IPO. Ads are clearly labeled and don't affect ChatGPT responses or expose private user conversations.

In the latest close session, IBM (IBM) was up +1.13% at $234.31. The stock exceeded the S&P 500, which registered a gain of 1.06% for the day. At the same time, the Dow added 1.18%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 1.4%.

Shares of the technology and consulting company have depreciated by 1.79% over the course of the past month, underperforming the Computer and Technology sector's gain of 3.99%, and the S&P 500's gain of 2.46%.

Analysts and investors alike will be keeping a close eye on the performance of IBM in its upcoming earnings disclosure. The company's upcoming EPS is projected at $2.9, signifying a 9.43% increase compared to the same quarter of the previous year. At the same time, our most recent consensus estimate is projecting a revenue of $16.88 billion, reflecting a 3.34% rise from the equivalent quarter last year.

For the annual period, the Zacks Consensus Estimates anticipate earnings of $12.33 per share and a revenue of $70.43 billion, signifying shifts of +6.38% and +4.28%, respectively, from the last year.

It is also important to note the recent changes to analyst estimates for IBM. Recent revisions tend to reflect the latest near-term business trends. Therefore, positive revisions in estimates convey analysts' confidence in the business performance and profit potential.

Research indicates that these estimate revisions are directly correlated with near-term share price momentum. To utilize this, we have created the Zacks Rank, a proprietary model that integrates these estimate changes and provides a functional rating system.

The Zacks Rank system, spanning from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), boasts an impressive track record of outperformance, audited externally, with #1 ranked stocks yielding an average annual return of +25% since 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection has moved 0.08% lower. IBM presently features a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold).

In terms of valuation, IBM is presently being traded at a Forward P/E ratio of 18.79. This valuation marks a discount compared to its industry average Forward P/E of 20.27.

It's also important to note that IBM currently trades at a PEG ratio of 2.21. The PEG ratio bears resemblance to the frequently used P/E ratio, but this parameter also includes the company's expected earnings growth trajectory. As of the close of trade yesterday, the Computer - Integrated Systems industry held an average PEG ratio of 0.61.

The Computer - Integrated Systems industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. At present, this industry carries a Zacks Industry Rank of 40, placing it within the top 17% of over 250 industries.
